But here... you know, I- I don't give a s***! They can bleep that.

Wear a peg on his nose or lose his wig

"Tony, would you rather eat a plate of maggots or go and get the Beach Boys?"
"It's in A to J." "Oh, pop pickers." Jesus Christ.

q: Ricky said he asked James Hyman whether Karl works hard. What did James reply?
a: "He doesn't work as hard as he used to"
f: Ricky insisted he wasn't calling Karl lazy, just "reporting speech". Karl: "Can't be bothered..."
ex: It's funny, right, because when he's moaning about-- I'd caught him out! He says he doesn't get a lunch break, he'd had over an hour... And then he went, I think he went quite early that night to get a hob or something. And I said to-- was…
And I said... "James, he's always complaining about working. Does he work hard?" And he went "Well... He doesn't work as hard as he used to..."
Play a record Karl, will you?
I don't really want to hit the start button now, I might do it in a bit. A bit lazy.

I'm not saying you're lazy! I'm saying that you know, maybe some people don't think you work as hard as you do. That's the way of the world. I'm not saying you don't work hard! Just reporting speech, really, on James Hyman? Calling him a…

q: While office-hunting, Ricky turned down one place that looked alright and had no porn shops nearby. What did Steve point out about it?

It had wild animals in the porch
It was next to a Starbucks

ex: It was Fifth Street or something like that. I went "Oh yeah," I went along to - "and I'll see you there in 20 minutes." I got there - you were there, if you remember. I looked around and I said to Steve, it looks alright, there's no - no -…
An office literally next to a brothel."
Right? When I go to work, I don't want to walk past prostitutes - call me old-fashioned.

q: Ricky once saw Leo Sayer on daytime TV giving clothes tips for the shorter man. What was his advice?
x: Always stand next to a child

ex: And err, in the link she went "well after the break, Leo Sayer's popping in to tell us about clothes for the shorter man."
I stayed tuned, he came on, he went-
Yeah. He went "wear a short jacket".
Optical illusion. You're going, "well that jacket, it couldn't be a foot long, cause that'd be mad. So it's two-foot long, so he's six foot."

His gum shield does all the talking

ex: See here's the good thing about the boxing thing, because er- there's no chance of me... you know, er slurring me words.
No, no. I already slurred my words.
So no- any damage will be totally fine. Oh dear.
The doctor's rushing in, "I think there might be some kind of concussion."
Jane just going, "No, that's just the way he talks."

q: Ricky explained how the bee manages to fly with such small wings. Roughly how many times a second did he say they beat?

So they have worked it out.
I know what you mean. I know what you mean it's- it's incredible that it can fly cause it has such small wings.
And it's a bee not a fly.
Yeah, but other than that, good point.

One of the most coveted of the awards.
In my- in my opinion the bronze is slightly better than the gold.
Well, a lot of people don't win the bronze, Rick. You gotta remember that- that there's not many people winning...
You see gold is- ya know- gold's got no intrinsic value it's just a currency. In my opinion bronze is better.

q: What did Jane say when she walked past and saw Ricky eating chicken legs in the bath?

ex: I do, I do eat in the bath. I mean, I-I- the second week of doing it, I was just eating in the bath. I was eating- I think I was eating chicken legs again. I’m eating in the bath. Jane walked past. Just looked in at me and she went…
Just me, a fat, Roman emperor eating--
Caligula, to be honest, is just too cool and impressive. You’re not Caligula. Old Man Steptoe.

ex: Right. Okay, then. What should we talk about, then? Um....Tracy--
Right, play a record and we’ll discuss this.
Tracey Emin! Sh- make your bed!
Make your bed! (giggles) Damien Hirst! Stop cutting up sharks an’ things. Um, Picasso...alright?

And that's all I'm— imagine saying that to a drill sergeant.
"I tell you what, I'm gonna give nearly a hundred."

ex: Well, from what I can work out, there's hundreds of em, millions of em, and they're all- and they're all shouting really loudly "what do we want? Peace! When do we want it? Now! What do we want? Peace!" I wanna go "ssh!"
We all want a bit of peace on a Saturday!

You know that thing I did with a tea towel? You put a tea towel round his head, right, tie it; I put a wooden spoon in, and you only have to turn it like a couple of inches, and it- it kills you dunnit?
"It really hurts yeah." So we'll be firing a cork at Karl's head, I'll be filming it for the website. That'll be brilliant

(Laughing) Sixpence None the Richer is quite good.

That surely puts you off the product a little bit.

So they, so they went through the things, right, and they went, “Tickets please,” and he just waved five tickets that he had, like that, he goes, “This is us, right,” and they went, “Well, can I have a look,” and went, “There’s only five…

q: At The Fat Duck in Bray, voted best restaurant in the world, what did they put in fussy Ricky's version of the snail porridge?
f: Ricky ate before he went, just in case, but said "they really accommodated me." On the way, Jonathan Ross phoned him: "Why are we taking you to this restaurant?"
ex: And uh, uh, me and Jane went along with him and Jane to The Fat Duck in Bray. It was voted the best restaurant in the world.

Okay. And um, it was incredible. I mean, it's a cross between a restaurant and sort of barnum. They take you, just, incredible, but all the way there, I'm thinking well I, I, I can't eat stuff in normal restaurants. I can't eat, I don't…
I, it was, I knew that one of their, um, signature dishes was snail porridge. So I'm thinking "I'm not gonna be able to eat anything here." So I'm thinking I had something to eat before I went.

I was thinking that they better not have mucked around the bread, right? Got there. Beautiful. Um, and uh, it was, it was, it was really quite fantastic. And, and I let them know straight away, um, that I was a philistine and they really…

They put um, mushrooms in my snail porridge, which was more risotto, and its tasting menus and that, and it was, it was, um, uh, really fantastic. But, Jonathan halfway through on the way there, I don't like travel well, on the way there…

q: Steve spotted a TV show called "I Survived a 200 Pound Tumor". What did Ricky reckon it really was?
a: A misprint for "I Survived a 200 Pound Tuna"
x: A misprint for "I Survived a 200 Pound Turnip"

Because it seems to me that you've got a 200 pound tumor you'll probably want to watch something else that'll take your mind off it Big Brother or whatever...
Well, I do I can't imagine what this is.
It must have been an error - 200 pound tumor?
It must have been a 200 pound tuna. It was probably someone fell in the water and it came at him.

Told the optician Steve was a famous DJ

And he went, “Uh what?” I went, “No, I’m jok- I‘m joking.” But, uh, yeah.

This is what's amazing about Karl, even though he's talking about things like mp3 players, computers, iPods, he sounds like he was found in a glacier and thawed out.

We're a couple of high school guys who find him and we're trying to ingratiate him in the gang, trying to pass him off of someone from the modern day.

And he threw a dice, he went, looked down, and went, and he said something like "I'm outside of...3 miles to Mummrah". And they went " Oh, well done". I wanted to say "what is this game".

q: Ricky mocked Karl's book for not being researched. Which country did one travel chapter cover, despite Karl writing 'I've never been there myself'?

What do you mean, making it up?
What is it that you're doing?
One of the chapters in your book about travel was Australia: "I've never been there myself." Forget it then! Throw it away!
Because you can still have thoughts on it.

q: According to Ricky, what was fashionable among rich Victorians?
a: Keeping a homeless "hobbit" living in their folly
x: Paying a beggar to sit on their roof
Hiring a chimney sweep to sing at dinner parties
Keeping a pickpocket in a birdcage
f: They were paid at the end if they stayed "for, like, three years", and guests were shown "our little Catweazel fella living in our folly."
ex: The rich sort of Victorians used to keep sort of homeless in their, as a little folly. And they used to pay them at the end if they stayed there for, like, three years.
What do you mean? They would pay them for what?
It was fashionable to have a little, like a little homeless little hobbit in your, in your outhouse. Seriously!
And what did they have, did they have to do anything for the money? Run, dance, fight tigers?
No, they just had to be there. No, they had to be there when they brought around. They'd go, "Look, that's our, that's our little Catweazel fella living in our folly."
And then they were. They got money, you know, at the end of it, there's just like, really rich sort of Victorians and stuff.

Milhouse. I think he looks like Mill House from the Simpsons.
